title: Linguine with Monkfish

media.caption: Clean the monkfish, removing the skin and the central bone.
Cut the monkfish into pieces and season lightly with salt.
Heat the extra virgin olive oil in a large pan and add the crushed garlic clove.
Add the halved cherry tomatoes to the pan and let them soften.
Continue sautéing the garlic and tomatoes until fragrant.
Place the monkfish pieces into the pan with the tomatoes and garlic.
Pour in the white wine and let it evaporate over high heat.
Season with salt and pepper, then lower the heat to simmer.
Cover the pan and let the fish cook gently, absorbing the flavors of the sauce.
Turn the fish pieces occasionally to ensure even cooking.
Check the fish for doneness, making sure it flakes easily with a fork.
Add the chopped parsley to the sauce for extra freshness.
When cooked, remove the fish and the cartilaginous bones, but put the flesh of the fish back into the pan, and continue cooking.
Place the drained linguine into the pan with the fish and cook for 1 minute over high heat, tossing to combine.
Plate the linguine with monkfish, garnishing with a little extra parsley and a drizzle of olive oil.
Serve the linguine with monkfish immediately while hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

healthBenefits.title: Lean Protein from Monkfish
healthBenefits.text: Monkfish is a low-fat, high-protein seafood that supports muscle repair and provides essential amino acids without excess saturated fat.

healthBenefits.title: Vitamin B12 & Selenium
healthBenefits.text: Monkfish is rich in vitamin B12 and selenium, nutrients important for nervous system function, thyroid health, and antioxidant defense.

healthBenefits.title: Heart-Healthy Olive Oil
healthBenefits.text: Extra virgin olive oil provides monounsaturated fats and polyphenols that help reduce inflammation and support cardiovascular health.

healthBenefits.title: Antioxidant Lycopene
healthBenefits.text: Cherry tomatoes are a good source of lycopene and vitamin C, antioxidants linked to reduced risk of heart disease and improved skin health.

healthBenefits.title: Immune-Supporting Garlic
healthBenefits.text: Garlic contains allicin, a compound with antimicrobial and cardiovascular benefits that may help lower blood pressure and cholesterol.

healthBenefits.title: Fresh Parsley Nutrients
healthBenefits.text: Parsley adds vitamin K and flavonoids that support bone health and provide additional antioxidant protection.

_ingredientsText:
300 gr of linguine pasta
1 medium sized monkfish  (cleaned)
8 cherry tomatoes, halved
1 clove of garlic 
1 tablespoon chopped parsley 
2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil 
½ cup white wine 
salt  
pepper (optional)
_preparationText:
1 - 14 fasi di preparazione del pesce
15 - When cooked, remove the fish and the cartilaginous bones, but put the flesh of the fish back into the pan, and continue cooking
 16 - In a separate pot, cook the linguine pasta in boiling, salted water until it is “al dente” and drain.
after Placing the linguine into the pan with the fish and cook for 1 minute over high heat.
